text: Write a method that returns two values by returning an object, rather than by using an out-parameter or two passes. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: ___                                     // a two-field carrier type, one line
for (int v : a) { ___; hi = Math.max(hi, v); }
answer: record MinMax(int min, int max) { }|lo = Math.min(lo, v)|new MinMax(lo, hi)
explanation: Verified: it prints MinMax[min=2, max=9]. This is the answer Chapter 11 promises and Chapter 22 delivers — the alternatives are an array whose indices you must remember, two passes doing the same work twice, or an out-parameter that hides a second output at the call site. One line declares a named type whose `toString` explains itself, which is why records changed what counts as reasonable for small local types.
